walkthrough: Goal: hide part of a coloured shape without erasing a pixel of it, reveal some of it again, try the opposite, compare with the mask off, hide part of a shading layer clipped to the shape, take a step back, and find it all again after reopening.

Entry: on an empty library (2880 x 1800, landscape) choose a blue in the colour panel, make the brush larger with the side bar's size slider and paint a solid blue shape on Layer 1 with the pen. Tap Layers: under Clipping Mask the footer now holds a row Mask, with the note White: shows all.

Add: tap Mask: a row Layer Mask (a sheet with a round window, its own eye) appears under Layer 1, one step to the right, outlined in deep ink: strokes now go to the mask. Layer 1's row loses its outline. The footer shows the mask's options instead of the layer's: Layer Mask, Black hides · white shows, Invert, Clear and a bin (Delete mask). The canvas does not change: a new mask is white.

Hide: close the panel with a tap on the canvas, choose black in the colour panel and paint a band across the shape: the blue disappears under the band and the white paper shows; nothing beside the shape changes. Reveal: tap Eraser, make it larger and rub across the middle of the band: the blue comes back there (the eraser paints white on a mask). Tap Brushes to paint again.
Invert: open Layers and tap Invert: now only the band's two ends show blue, everything else of the shape is hidden; the mask's row says Inverted. Tap Invert again: back as it was.

Off and on: tap the mask row's eye (Turn mask off): the whole shape shows, the row says Off, and Layer 1's row takes the outline again (an off mask takes no strokes). Tap it again (Turn mask on): the band is hidden again; tap the Layer Mask row to paint on it again, then Layer 1's row to paint on the layer.

Clipping: tap the plus (Layer 2 above Layer 1), Clipping Mask, and close the panel; choose red and paint across the shape: red shows only where the blue shows, so not in the hidden band (the base's mask shapes its chain). Open Layers and tap Mask: Layer 2 gets its own mask, outlined. Close the panel, choose black and paint a short stroke down through the red: the red goes there and the blue under it stays (the clipping layer's mask hides only itself).
Undo in the side bar: the red is back where the last stroke hid it; redo: hidden again. Every mask change (add, invert, off, on, each stroke) is one step; choosing the mask or the layer is none.
Reopen after the system closed the app: the same picture pixel for pixel; Layers shows both masks under their layers and Layer 2's mask still outlined.

Failure and cancel: Mask is grey on a layer that has one; Invert and Clear are grey and the row cannot be chosen while the mask is off; Transform while the mask is outlined refuses with a notice (a mask does not move; tap the layer to move its paint). Not here: masks on groups, applying a mask into the layer, moving a mask, a separate mask grey slider, swiping a mask row.
